items.subject: Board prices aging inside a fresh file
items.premise_verified: TRUE, all four legs re-checked against live data before acting. (A) REACHABILITY: check-ad-cycles.ps1 at HEAD carried `$fcArgs = @(` at line 455, inside the `if (-not $NoPull) {` that opens at 382 and closes at 480 - read in the source, not inferred. The string '] ff-carry:' appears 0 times in 1,771 lines of ad-cycle-log.txt, and coverage-ledger.json's audit-ff-carry row is as_of 2026-08-29 17:21:15 (examined 45 of 558), which is the 4-days-vs-limit-3 STALE the 08:24 cycle printed. (B) RESCUE FLOOR: the rescue-terms headers reproduce the plan's numbers exactly - Aldi 359 of 359 traced, Fareway 141 of 131, Sam's Club 377 of 374, Walmart 502 of 500, i.e. 1,379 eligible and 1,364 traced against a 1,517 baseline = 10.1% under a 10% tolerance. (C) MEASURED BEYOND THE PLAN, and it confirms the blast radius rather than widening it: only ONE scheduled task per day reaches the moved block. capture-run.ps1:502 reads `$runDownstream = (-not $NoDownstream) -and (($Kind -ne 'ad') -or $Downstream)`, so the 07:00 -Kind ad task captures only and never calls check-ad-cycles; the 09:30 task is capture-watchdog.ps1, which does not call it at all; bakers-daily-scan is not a scheduled task. So the 08:00 daily chain is the single caller, which is exactly one ~45-probe Freshop burst a day, as the plan predicted. $serverDue is unconditionally true whenever any store is method=server (:334-335), so the new position inside `if ($serverDue)` runs on every one of those.
items.deviation: Two, both small. (1) The plan's surface_fix names the baseline as grocery/out/coverage-baseline.json; the file is at grocery/coverage-baseline.json (out/ holds the LEDGER, the repo root holds the BASELINE). Accepted there. (2) The accept had to be scoped `-Accept -AcceptLower -Check build-rescue-worklist`, because -Accept alone refuses to lower and a bare -AcceptLower would have lowered six other dropped rows that are not in breach (audit-everyday-mismatch, audit-ff-carry 464->45, guards/13-recipe, guards/3-pin-derivable, guards/3-pin-identity, guards/4-factor). The run named all six as HELD and lowered exactly one row, 1517 -> 1364. The reason is written into that row's `why` before the accept, not after. The 10% tolerance was not touched. audit-ff-carry's own floor stays at 464. NOT SHIPPED, and it is the plan's own live proof rather than an omission: the 2026-09-03 08:24 coverage-cycle line and the first '] ff-carry:' entry in ad-cycle-log.txt. audit-ff-carry was deliberately NOT run by hand today - it would have spent ~45 Freshop probes outside a capture window, against the do_not_touch on the Family Fare shard cadence. The ledger therefore still reads STALE for that one check tonight, which is expected and is the last thing left to watch.
items.resolution_note_as_written_by_the_review: The row-age page was the Baker's expired ad (same condition as 68183c, resolved by the 09:07 capture); every store's rows are dated, none exceed the 90-day carry, and no row claims a date newer than its file (checked at all 7 stores, not just the 2 the as_of-evidence guard watches). Two ledger findings folded in: audit-ff-carry has not run from the scheduled chain since 2026-08-23 because it lives inside the pull block every caller skips with -NoPull (moved out, pinned by a structural test); build-rescue-worklist's floor moved on 08-23/24 when Fareway's shop markdowns became sale-typed (402 -> 141 everyday cells), re-baselined with that reason.

items.deviation: The plan expects new-contested = 1 after the rebuild. It came back NINE, because the 09:07 Baker's ad and the 09:19/09:24 Walmart and Aldi captures brought names the reviewer's 08:03 board did not contain. I resolved each by hand before accepting anything. Seven are order-dependence between two defensible readings and are what the flag is for: Nalley beef stew (beef-stew over jarred-gravy, correct), 'California Yellow or White Peaches or Nectarines' (peaches over nectarines, an either/or ad row), 'Gourmet Peaches With Ginger Flavor' (peaches over fresh-ginger), 'Kroger Side Dish, Macaroni & Cheese or Homestyle Mashed Potatoes' (mac-and-cheese over instant-mashed-potatoes), the Lay's/Tostitos either/or (tortilla-chips over potato-chips), 'Raspberries or Blackberries' (raspberries over blackberries - the only one of the nine that holds a cell, Baker's $0.4983/oz, and both readings are the same 6 oz at the same $2.99 so the number is right either way), and the plan's own Southern Grove peanuts/sea-salt case. TWO WERE GENUINELY WRONG and are the same bare-token class this item exists to fix: 'Best Foods Made with Cage Free Eggs Light Mayonnaise' and 'Sir Kensington's Classic Mayonnaise ... Made with Free-Range Eggs' were owned by eggs, and 'Bridgford Sweet Baby Ray's Honey Barbecue Beef Jerky' was owned by honey. I fenced them (eggs.exclude += \bmayonnaise\b, honey.exclude += \bjerky\b) rather than accept, because -Accept blesses every pending contested flag permanently - the contested-flag-baselined-away class - and these two would have been silenced for good. After the fences new-contested is 7, all order-dependence, and only then was the baseline accepted (18,643 names, 384 contested, drift-vs-engine 0). Never -Force.

items.subject: Grocery: 1 board cell(s) sit in the wrong store department - 2026-09-02
items.premise_verified: TRUE, and the class fix reproduced the reviewer's simulation. Before: aisle-test returned BLOCK on gruyere @ Family Fare for the Aidells chicken sausage at $0.5825/oz. After: aisle-test -LiveBoard is 408 ALLOW and 0 BLOCK, and the cell is Smoky Park Smoked Gruyere 8 Oz at $0.9988/oz - the exact number the plan predicted. The 21 exempt ids were checked to exist before the bake (all 21 do) and to carry no pre-existing sausage exclude that would block a re-landing. apply-category-excludes reported +513 patterns across 513 commodities, which reconciles exactly: 533 commodities sit in the three scoped categories and 20 of the 21 exemptions are inside them (dog-treats is category Pet, which no apply block covers). Of the 25 sausage movers exactly ONE held a board cell, checked by name against every store item on the board, and it is this one.
items.deviation: THE BAKE TOOL BREAKS AN ARMED GATE, AND HAD TO BE FIXED BEFORE IT COULD BE RUN. apply-category-excludes.ps1 wrote commodities.json with `($commods | ConvertTo-Json -Depth 6) | Set-Content -Encoding UTF8`. ConvertTo-Json emits non-ASCII characters LITERALLY - the \uXXXX escapes decode on read and never come back - and Set-Content prepends a BOM. commodities.json is in audit-json-encoding.ps1's ASCII_PINNED list, where a single non-ASCII byte is a hard finding, and ops\run-gates.ps1 runs that check. MEASURED on a scratch copy of the live tree before touching anything: a NO-OP bake ('+0 patterns across 0 commodities') still rewrote the file with a BOM and 84 literal non-ASCII bytes, turning 'jalape[n\u00f1]o' into 'jalape[nn-tilde]o' and unescaping the crema, creme-fraiche, rose, entree and sazon classes. That is the exact corruption the 2026-08-31 mojibake pass was written to end: it fixed this script's READ (-Encoding UTF8) and left its WRITE, so the guard and the sanctioned tool that violates it have been shipping side by side.
